examples.en: A strange noise is coming from the boiler room.
I opened the boiler room door and checked the boiler.
In our house, we put the washing machine in the boiler room.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 보일러실이 얼지 않게 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: In winter you have to be careful that the boiler room doesn't freeze.

examples.ko: 보일러실 안은 좁아서 물건을 두기 어려워요.
examples.en: The inside of the boiler room is narrow, so it's hard to keep things there.

examples.ko: 아저씨가 보일러실로 들어가서 보일러를 고쳐 주셨어요.
examples.en: The repairman went into the boiler room and fixed the boiler.

explain: 한국 집에서 바닥 난방을 하는 보일러를 두는 작은 공간이에요. 베란다 옆에 있거나 '다용도실'과 같은 곳을 쓰기도 해요. 보일러가 고장 나면 '보일러가 고장 났어요'라고 하고 수리 기사를 불러요.

phrases.en: The cleaning tools are in the boiler room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 어디에 있는지 말할 때 '에 있다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '에 있다' to say where something is.
phrases.en_equiv: to be in the boiler room

phrases.en: It is a little warm inside the boiler room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방 안쪽 상태를 말할 때 '안'을 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 안 to talk about the inside of the room.

phrases.en: The washing machine is in the utility room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보일러실과 같은 곳을 쓰기도 하는 집 안의 작은 공간이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A small utility space in a home that is sometimes the same place as the boiler room.

explain_en: It is the small space in a Korean home where the boiler for floor heating is kept. It may be next to the balcony or the same place as a '다용도실' (utility room). If the boiler breaks, you say '보일러가 고장 났어요' and call a repair person.

examples.en: There is a bidet in the bathroom at my house.
A bidet is comfortable because the water is warm.
I installed a new bidet on the toilet.
The bidet water pressure is too strong.
Water is leaking from the bidet.

examples.ko: 이 비데로 바꾸고 나서 아주 만족해요.
examples.en: I am very satisfied since I switched to this bidet.

explain: 한국에서 비데는 보통 변기에 붙어 있는 기기를 말하고, 변기와는 다른 물건이에요. 설치는 '비데를 달다', '비데를 설치하다'라고 해요. 고장 나면 '비데가 고장 나다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I installed a bidet in my new home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '설치하다'보다 일상적으로 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more everyday word than '설치하다'.

phrases.en: The bidet broke, so I called for a repair.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계가 작동하지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when a machine stops working.

phrases.en: The bidet water is too cold.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비데에서 나오는 물을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the water that comes from the bidet.

explain_en: In Korea a '비데' usually means a device attached to a toilet, so it is a different thing from the toilet itself. You say '비데를 달다' or '비데를 설치하다' to install it, and '비데가 고장 나다' when it breaks.

examples.en: I hung the blanket on the clothesline in the yard.
The clothesline is shaking hard in the strong wind.

examples.ko: 빨랫줄 가득 널린 수건이 벌써 말랐어요.
examples.en: The towels hanging all over the clothesline have already dried.

examples.ko: 비가 올 것 같아서 빨랫줄에서 옷을 걷었어요.
examples.en: It looked like rain, so I took the clothes down from the line.
I put up another clothesline on the balcony.
Sparrows are sitting on the clothesline.

explain: '빨래를 빨랫줄에 널다', '빨래를 걷다'처럼 함께 쓰는 동사를 같이 알아 두세요. 요즘 아파트에서는 줄보다 '건조대'에 빨래를 너는 집도 많아요.

phrases.en: I hung the wet towel on the clothesline.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄에 빨래를 걸어 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when hanging laundry on a line to dry.

phrases.en: The laundry hanging on the line is swaying in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄에 널려 있는 빨래를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe laundry that is hanging on a line.

phrases.en: My father tied up a clothesline in the yard for us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빨래를 널 줄을 설치할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when setting up a line for hanging laundry.

explain_en: Learn it with its verbs: '빨래를 빨랫줄에 널다' (hang) and '빨래를 걷다' (take down). In today's apartments, many homes hang laundry on a '건조대' (drying rack) instead of a line.

examples.ko: 목욕탕에 갈 때는 소지품을 사물함에 넣어 두세요.
examples.en: When you go to the bathhouse, put your belongings in a locker.
My gym clothes are in my locker.
I lost my locker key, so I went to the office.
I can't remember my locker number.
This locker opens only when you enter the password.

examples.ko: 헬스장에서 개인 사물함을 한 달 신청했어요.
examples.en: I signed up for a personal locker at the gym for a month.

explain: 학교, 헬스장, 목욕탕처럼 내 물건을 넣어 두는 칸을 말해요. '로커'라고도 하지만 일상에서는 '사물함'이 자주 쓰여요. 지하철역이나 터미널에서 짐을 잠깐 맡기는 곳은 보통 '물품보관함'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I put my bag in the gym locker.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영어에서 온 말로, 헬스장이나 수영장에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A loanword from English, common at gyms and pools.

phrases.en: I lost my locker key.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사물함을 잠그고 여는 열쇠를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the key that locks and opens a locker.

phrases.en: I cleaned out my locker before vacation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 학교에서 사물함 안의 물건을 치울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for tidying up the things in a locker, especially at school.

explain_en: It is the compartment where you keep your own things at school, a gym or a bathhouse. '로커' is also used, but '사물함' is common in daily life. The place in a subway station or terminal where you briefly leave luggage is usually called '물품보관함'.

examples.ko: 시곗바늘이 오후 네 시를 가리키고 있어요.
examples.en: The clock hands are pointing to four in the afternoon.
The clock hands stopped, so I changed the battery.
I can hear the clock hands ticking along.

examples.ko: 아이가 시곗바늘 보는 법을 배우고 있어요.
examples.en: The child is learning how to read the clock hands.
During the exam, I kept staring at the clock hands.
It looks like the clock hands are going backwards.

explain: 짧은 바늘은 '시침', 긴 바늘은 '분침', 가는 바늘은 '초침'이라고 해요. 시곗바늘은 이 바늘들을 모두 부르는 말이에요.

phrases.en: The hands of the clock turn slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시계가 움직이는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the clock hands moving.

phrases.en: Looking at the clock hands, it is already ten o'clock.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시계로 시간을 확인할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking the time on a clock.
phrases.en_equiv: to look at the clock hands

phrases.en: I turned the clock hands forward one hour.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시계 시간을 직접 맞출 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when setting a clock by hand.

explain_en: The short hand is the '시침', the long hand is the '분침', and the thin hand is the '초침'. 시곗바늘 is the general word for all of them.

examples.en: I put a pencil holder on the desk.
There are ten ballpoint pens in the pencil holder.
I found a pretty cup to use as a pencil holder.
The pencil holder fell over and all the pens spilled out.
There are scissors in the pencil holder too.
I made this pencil holder myself out of paper.

explain: 책상 위에 세워 두고 연필, 볼펜, 가위 같은 것을 꽂아 두는 통이에요. 가방에 넣고 다니는 '필통'과 달라요. 이름은 연필이지만 다른 문구도 함께 꽂아요.

phrases.en: Please stick the pen in the pencil holder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 세워서 넣어 둘 때 '꽂다'를 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '꽂다' is the verb used when putting things in upright.
phrases.en_equiv: to put in the pencil holder

phrases.en: I bought a pencil holder to put on my desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문구를 정리하려고 물건을 살 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when buying something to organize stationery.

phrases.en: There are scissors in the pencil holder on the desk, too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연필꽂이가 놓인 자리를 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say where the pencil holder sits.

explain_en: It is a container that stands on a desk and holds pencils, pens and scissors. It differs from a '필통' (pencil case), which you carry in a bag. Despite the name, it holds other stationery too.

examples.ko: 자동문 앞에 서면 문이 저절로 열려요.
examples.en: If you stand in front of the automatic door, it opens by itself.

examples.ko: 자동문이 고장 나서 지금은 수동으로 열어야 해요.
examples.en: The automatic door is broken, so now we have to open it by hand.

examples.ko: 아기가 자동문에 손이 끼지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful that the baby's hand doesn't get caught in the automatic door.

examples.ko: 마트 입구는 자동문이라서 카트를 밀고 들어가기 편해요.
examples.en: The store entrance is an automatic door, so it's easy to push a cart in.
A cold wind blew as soon as I passed the automatic door.

examples.ko: 이 건물은 자동문이 아니라서 문을 직접 밀어야 해요.
examples.en: This building has no automatic door, so you have to push the door yourself.

explain: '자동문이 열리다/닫히다'처럼 문이 스스로 움직일 때는 '열리다·닫히다'를 써요. 사람이 직접 여는 건 '열다'예요. 고장 났을 때는 '수동으로 열다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: If you go up to it, the automatic door opens.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문이 스스로 움직일 때 '열리다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '열리다' is used when the door moves by itself.

phrases.en: I went in before the automatic door closed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 닫힐 때 '닫히다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '닫히다' is used when it closes by itself.

phrases.en: The automatic door was broken, so I opened it manually.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 직접 열 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person opens it directly.

explain_en: When the door moves by itself, use '열리다/닫히다', as in '자동문이 열리다'. When a person opens it, use '열다'. When it is broken, you say '수동으로 열다' (open it manually).

examples.en: At Christmas the streets are decorated with lights.
The room was prettily decorated with flowers.
Paintings are displayed on the wall.
I saw that the cake was decorated with strawberries.
The party place will be decorated with balloons.

examples.ko: 예쁘게 장식되어 있는 카페라서 사진을 많이 찍었어요.
examples.en: The cafe was prettily decorated, so I took lots of photos.

explain: '장식하다'는 하는 사람이 있고, '장식되다'는 꾸며진 결과를 말해요. '~으로 장식되다'는 어떤 재료로 꾸몄는지 말할 때 써요. 일상에서는 '꾸미다', '꾸며져 있다'도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The room decorated with flowers is pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꾸며진 모습을 명사 앞에서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used before a noun to describe something that has been decorated.

phrases.en: The front of the shop is decorated with balloons.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 꾸며져 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of already being decorated.

phrases.en: The street was decorated splendidly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 띄게 예쁘게 꾸며졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is decorated in a fancy, eye-catching way.

explain_en: Passive: something is decorated; focus on the result, not the doer (꽃으로 장식되다) 장식하다 has a person doing it, while 장식되다 describes the decorated result. '~으로 장식되다' tells what the decoration is made of. In daily talk 꾸미다 and 꾸며져 있다 are also common.

en: to be charged; to be recharged; to be filled up

examples.en: The phone was charged all night.
The battery charges up to 80 percent.
My transit card wasn't topped up, so I couldn't ride.
Please don't play games while it's charging.
When points are added, a text message comes.
Unplug it after it has charged enough.

explain: '충전하다'는 사람이 하는 일이고 '충전되다'는 에너지나 돈이 채워지는 상태를 말해요. 휴대폰 배터리, 교통카드, 포인트에 자주 써요. '쉬면서 에너지를 충전하다'처럼 사람에게 비유로 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: The phone is charging right now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 채워지는 중이라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it is being filled at this moment.

phrases.en: The cable is broken, so it won't charge.
phrases.nuance_ko: 충전되지 않는 문제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about a problem when it won't charge.

phrases.en: The battery is fully charged.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가득 찬 상태가 됐다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it has become completely full.

explain_en: Be refilled or charged — batteries, fuel, energy, physical filling. 충전하다 is what a person does, while 충전되다 describes energy or money being filled in. It is common for phone batteries, transit cards and points. People also use 충전하다 figuratively, as in recharging energy by resting.

examples.en: I drank coffee on the cafe terrace.
Our house has a small terrace.
I put several flowerpots on the terrace.
The weather was nice, so I stepped out onto the terrace.
The terrace is nice because of the cool breeze.
I want to move to a house with a terrace.

explain: '베란다'와 비슷해요. 카페나 식당의 바깥 자리도 테라스라고 불러요.

phrases.en: Shall we sit at a terrace seat?
phrases.nuance_ko: 카페나 식당의 바깥 자리를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for outdoor seats at a cafe or restaurant.

phrases.en: I met a friend at a cafe with a terrace.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바깥 자리가 있는 카페를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cafe that has an outdoor seating area.

phrases.en: I want to live in a house with a terrace.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에 딸린 테라스를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a terrace that belongs to a home.

explain_en: It is similar to 베란다. The outdoor seating of a cafe or restaurant is also called 테라스.

examples.ko: 다 마신 페트병은 재활용 통에 넣어 주세요.
examples.en: Please put empty plastic bottles in the recycling bin.

examples.ko: 페트병도 재활용이 돼요? — 네, 라벨을 떼고 버리세요.
examples.en: Can plastic bottles be recycled too? — Yes, remove the label and throw it away.
I filled a plastic bottle with water and put it in the freezer.
I flatten plastic bottles before throwing them away.
I made a flowerpot out of an empty plastic bottle.
Plastic bottles are light, so they're easy to carry.

explain: 물이나 음료가 담긴 투명한 플라스틱 병을 말해요. 한국에서는 분리배출할 때 라벨을 떼고 헹궈서 버리라고 안내해요. '병' 앞에 붙여 쓰는 한 단어예요.

phrases.en: I remove the label from an empty plastic bottle before throwing it away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다 마시고 비어 있는 병을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a bottle that is empty after drinking.

phrases.en: I throw plastic bottles into the recycling bin.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분리배출을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase when talking about recycling.
phrases.en_equiv: to throw away a plastic bottle

phrases.en: I put water in a plastic bottle and take it with me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병 안에 액체를 넣을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you put liquid into a bottle.
phrases.en_equiv: to put into a plastic bottle

explain_en: It means the clear plastic bottles that hold water or drinks. In Korea, recycling guides tell you to remove the label and rinse it before disposal. It is written as one word, attached to '병'.

en: to be opened; to be spread out; to unfold

examples.ko: 우산이 잘 펴지지 않아서 비를 맞았어요.
examples.en: The umbrella wouldn't open properly, so I got wet.

examples.ko: 다리미로 누르면 주름이 쫙 펴지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: It seems the wrinkles smooth out when you press them with an iron.

examples.ko: 구겨진 종이가 물에 닿으면 저절로 펴지기도 해요.
examples.en: Crumpled paper sometimes flattens out by itself when it touches water.

examples.ko: 마음이 놓이니까 찡그린 얼굴이 펴지고 웃음이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Once I felt relieved, my frowning face relaxed and I smiled.

examples.ko: 이 소파는 버튼을 누르면 침대처럼 펴지는 거예요.
examples.en: This sofa unfolds like a bed when you press the button.
I couldn't straighten my back, so I went to the hospital.

explain: '펴다'는 내가 펴는 것이고, '펴지다'는 접히거나 구겨진 것이 저절로 또는 어떤 힘으로 펴진다는 느낌이에요. 주름, 우산, 허리, 얼굴처럼 접히거나 굽은 것에 잘 써요.

phrases.example: 취직한 뒤로 우리 집 형편이 많이 펴졌어요.
phrases.en: Since I got a job, our family's circumstances have improved a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어렵던 살림이 나아져서 여유가 생겼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that a tight financial situation has improved and there is some breathing room.

explain_en: Folded or wrinkled things flatten out (종이가 펴지다) '펴다' is you opening something, while '펴지다' is the folded or crumpled thing becoming open or flat on its own or by some force. It suits wrinkles, umbrellas, backs and faces, things that are folded or bent.

t90.ax: The umbrella wouldn't open properly, so I got wet.

examples.en: The cup fell on the floor and broke.

examples.ko: 창문이 깨어져서 방 안으로 바람이 들어와요.
examples.en: The window is broken, so wind comes into the room.

examples.ko: 약속이 깨어지면 서로 마음이 많이 아파요.
examples.en: When a promise is broken, both people get hurt.
I carried the plate carefully in case it broke.
The moment the dream was shattered, I felt so empty.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 사이가 깨어지지 않았으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope the relationship between the two of them doesn't break.

explain: '깨지다'와 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때는 줄여서 '깨져요, 깨졌어요'라고 많이 해요. 컵이나 유리 같은 물건뿐 아니라 약속, 꿈, 분위기, 사이가 무너질 때도 써요. 잠에서 '깨다'와는 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: The cup fell and broke.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깨어졌어요'를 줄인 말로, 말할 때 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The shortened form of '깨어졌어요', used more in speech.

phrases.en: Glass breaks easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건이 약하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say an object is fragile.

phrases.en: Something suddenly came up, so the plan fell through.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건뿐 아니라 약속이 지켜지지 않을 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Not just objects; also used when a promise or plan falls through.

explain_en: To shatter or crack into pieces, like glass or a cup; also plans (계획이 깨어지다). It means the same as '깨지다', and in speech people often shorten it to '깨져요' or '깨졌어요'. It is used for objects like cups and glass, and also for promises, dreams, moods and relationships falling apart. Don't confuse it with '깨다' (to wake up from sleep).

t90.ax: The cup fell on the floor and broke.

en: to remain; to be left; to be left behind

examples.en: I was scared because I was left alone at home.
A lot of food has been left over.
The person who is left last turns off the lights.
All that was left to him was an old watch.
All my friends left and only I was left behind.
A note had been left on the desk.

explain: '남다'는 저절로 남는 것이고, '남기다'는 누가 일부러 남기는 것이에요. '남겨지다'는 남기다의 피동으로, 내가 원하지 않았는데 남은 느낌이 강해요. 특히 사람이 혼자 두고 간 곳에 '남겨지다'라고 하면 쓸쓸한 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: A note has been left on the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가 둔 것이 그대로 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something someone left that is still there.

phrases.en: I was the only one left in the classroom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 혼자 남은 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a past situation of being left behind.

phrases.en: I don't want to be left alone.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하지 않는데 혼자 남는 상황을 싫어한다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say you don't want to be left behind against your will.
phrases.en_equiv: don't want to be left behind

explain_en: Everyday passive, someone or something is left, often a lonely feeling. '남다' is something that remains by itself, and '남기다' is someone deliberately leaving it. '남겨지다' is the passive of 남기다 and feels like being left against your will. Used for a person left alone, it sounds lonely.

t90.ax: A lot of food has been left over.
